content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast tends to peak too early and then underreact to subsequent price corrections.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds high forecasts longer than actual price behavior suggests.
- Overshoots occur after sharp upward moves; model fails to adjust downward quickly enough.
- Late-period forecasts (last 5–10 days) show underestimation, particularly when true prices are rising sharply.
- Model exhibits lag in recognizing sustained upward trends; often misses momentum shifts.
- Forecasts are overly smooth; fail to capture volatility clustering or sudden reversals.
- When true price rises sharply, model initially overreacts and then undercorrects.
- Model tends to underestimate the magnitude of price spikes in the final 10–15 days of the forecast window.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward if recent 5-day average is rising faster than 30-day average.
